description: A stereo reverb built from an eight-line feedback delay network with diffusion inside the loop and two detuned LFOs moving every read tap

params.text: Scales the whole network from a small room to an enormous space
Sets the reverberation time, 0.2 seconds at the bottom of the knob and rising to an endless tail at the very top
Sets how thickly the allpass diffusion smears the input before it reaches the network
Sets the rate of the two LFOs that move the delay taps, from 0.05Hz to 8Hz
Sets how far the LFOs move the delay taps, which is what gives the tail its chorusing
Delays the signal before it reaches the reverb, up to 250ms
Rolls the low end out of the tail, from 10Hz to 500Hz
Rolls the top off the tail, from 500Hz down to 20kHz
Blends the reverb against the dry signal
Holds the tail forever, cutting the input off from the network

inputs.text: Moves the size, 10V sweeping its whole range
Moves the reverberation time, 10V sweeping its whole range
Moves the wet and dry blend, 10V sweeping its whole range
The left channel in, which also feeds the right channel when the jack beside it is empty
A high gate holds the tail forever, cutting the input off from the network; it reads high above 1V and low below 0.1V

outputs.text: The left channel out; with the right output unpatched this jack carries the two channels summed to mono

notes: the eclipse on the panel is driven by the audio: its corona brightens with the energy in the tail and embers drift from the rim with the incoming signal
